info.title: PostGrip Agent API
info.description: Canonical HTTP contract consumed by the PostGrip Agent SDKs. Workflow replay, request signing, archive streaming, and WebSocket framing remain SDK runtime concerns.

get.description: Returns a fixed ok status without touching the store. This is the only route that bypasses authentication entirely, so an uptime monitor can call it with no credential.
Reports readiness along with current task, workflow, schedule, and namespace counts. Unlike the liveness probe this route requires a credential.

get.summary: List namespaces visible to the caller
get.description: Scoped to the tenant the credential resolves to, and narrowed further to the agent's namespace allow-list when called with an agent session.

post.description: Any tenantId in the body is ignored and replaced with the tenant the credential resolves to.

post.summary: Purge finished tasks and workflows across every tenant
post.description: Deletes every succeeded or failed task, and every workflow that is not running, last updated before the retention cutoff -- along with their events and history. Irreversible, and deliberately not scoped to one tenant: a tenant-scoped credential is refused rather than narrowed.

get.description: Filters by namespace, queue, type, and state within the caller's tenant, then sorts and paginates.

post.description: Returns 202 with the created task. Any tenantId in the body is replaced with the tenant the credential resolves to.

get.description: A task belonging to another tenant is reported as 404 rather than 403, so identifiers cannot be probed across tenant boundaries.
Returns the task's full event history in order -- lease, start, heartbeat, stdout, stderr, and terminal events. This endpoint is not paginated.

post.description: Returns 202. Any tenantId in the body is replaced with the tenant the credential resolves to.

patch.description: A partial update: only the fields present in the body are changed.

delete.description: Returns the deleted schedule with 200 rather than an empty 204; the record moves to the deleted state.

post.description: Stops the schedule firing without deleting it, and returns the updated schedule.
Fires the schedule out of band from its spec. The next scheduled run is unaffected.

post.summary: Backfill a schedule across a time range
post.description: Enqueues one task per scheduled instant between the requested start and end. A range that would exceed the server's per-request cap is rejected outright rather than silently truncated.

parameters.name: search.*
parameters.description: Search-attribute filter; replace * with the attribute name.

get.summary: Count workflow executions matching a filter
get.description: Applies the same filters as the list operation and returns only the count. Paging parameters are ignored.

parameters.name: search.*
parameters.description: Search-attribute filter; replace * with the attribute name.

get.description: Returns the latest run of the workflow.

post.summary: Send a signal to a running workflow
post.description: Returns 202 with the appended history event. A signal also releases the workflow's blocked task, which is how a task that parked itself resumes. Signalling a workflow that is no longer running fails.

post.summary: Signal a workflow, starting it first if none is running
post.description: Starts a new execution of workflowType when no running one exists, then delivers the signal. A workflowId in the body takes precedence over the one in the path.

post.summary: Request cooperative cancellation of a workflow
post.description: Asks the workflow to stop at its next cancellation point. Use terminate for an execution that does not cooperate.
Stops the execution immediately, without giving workflow code a chance to clean up.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new agent session
post.description: The refresh token in the body is itself the credential, so this operation carries no bearer token. Rotation is single-use: presenting a token that has already been rotated revokes the whole token family.

get.summary: Long-poll for the next leased task or lifecycle directive
get.description: Blocks up to wait_seconds and returns 200 with an empty object -- not 204 -- when nothing is available. A queued lifecycle directive (upgrade, log level, attest) is returned in place of a task, and an agent that has been removed receives 410 carrying a shutdown directive.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Current agent runtime version used to enforce upgrade policy.

parameters.name: log_level
parameters.description: Current agent log level used to synchronize runtime configuration.

parameters.name: capabilities
parameters.description: Runtime and isolation capabilities advertised by the agent. The server accepts repeated or comma-separated values.

post.description: Extends the lease and appends a heartbeat event. The task must currently be leased to the calling agent.

post.summary: Append an event to a leased task
post.description: Records one progress, stdout, stderr, or milestone event and returns 202. It does not extend the lease -- send a heartbeat for that.
Terminal. Stores the result, releases the lease, and advances the owning workflow. Secret values drawn from the task's environment are masked out of the stored result.

post.summary: Park a leased task until its workflow is signalled
post.description: Non-terminal: the task moves to blocked and its lease is released, so it is not retried and no longer counts against the agent. It resumes only when its workflow receives a signal.
Terminal. Records the error, releases the lease, and drives the workflow's retry or failure handling. Error text is masked for secrets before it is stored.

get.description: Returns the tenant's live sandboxes. Deleted sandboxes are omitted here but remain fetchable by id.

post.description: Records the desired sandbox and returns 201. Provisioning is asynchronous, so the returned record is not yet running. Names must be unique per tenant among live sandboxes.

delete.description: Sets desired state to deleted and returns 202 with the updated record. Teardown is asynchronous and completes when the assigned agent reports it.

post.description: Sets desired state to running and returns 202. The returned record still carries the previous observed state; a sandbox is ready only once observedState is running and observedGeneration has caught up with generation.
Sets desired state to stopped and returns 202. The assigned agent applies it asynchronously.

post.summary: Mint a single-use ticket for an interactive session
post.description: Creates a pending pty or exec session and returns its ticket exactly once -- only a hash of it is stored. The ticket is short-lived and is redeemed against the connect operation. The sandbox must already be running.

The request body is a raw gzipped tar stream, not a multipart form. Repository and revision metadata travel in the X-PostGrip-Repository and X-PostGrip-Revision headers. Storage is content-addressed, so re-uploading identical bytes returns the existing record rather than creating a new one.

get.summary: Attach to an interactive session over WebSocket
get.description: Upgrades to a WebSocket carrying raw, unframed stdio; stdout and stderr are interleaved on one stream and there is no resize channel. The process exit code arrives as the WebSocket close status offset by 4000, not in the stream itself.

managementToken.description: Management token issued by the PostGrip console.

globalAdminToken.description: Service-level administration token accepted only by global administration endpoints.

agentSession.description: Delegated short-lived agent session. Signed operations also carry the PostGrip Ed25519 request-signing headers.

AgentIdQuery.name: agent_id
AgentIdQuery.description: Compatibility identifier; authenticated requests derive the agent from the session token.
